Judgment

This criminal appeal has been preferred to challenge the judgment dated 22.5.1998 delivered by Additional Sessions Judge, Raisen, in Sessions Trial No.88/1997 whereby the appellants (hereinafter referred to as "accused persons") were convicted of the offence of Section 376(1) IPC and sentenced to four years rigorous imprisonment.

2. Brief facts relevant for the decision of this criminal appeal are that two inmates of Rajkumari Bai Bal Niketan Sanstha, Jabalpur (for short, "Sanstha") left their Sanstha on 4.1.1997 and in search of job they travelled from Jabalpur to Mandideep; both the accused persons met and stopped them at Mandideep; both the girls scolded the accused, but later when they offered to search a rented house,
the girls accompanied them; a rented house was taken in Shantinagar where both the girls stayed;
on the same day at around 9:00 p.m. accused persons arrived at their place and despite their resentment, the y committed rape with girls; the girls 2 CRA-1339-1998 were later given shelter by police of Mandideep and brought them back to their Sanstha in Jabalpur on 12.1.1997; both the girls informed the working committee of that Sanstha about the commission of rape upon which the Superintendent of Sanstha gave a written complaint; an FIR was registered and the matter was investigated; upon its completion, the charge-sheet was filed and the accused persons after facing the trial were convicted and sentenced as aforesaid.
3. The grounds raised in this criminal appeal are that both the prosecutrix were more than 16 years of age at the time of alleged crime; no external or internal injury was found on their person; there was no FSL report to support the conviction; there was an exceptional delay in reporting the matter Ajay @ Ajju & Anr. vs The State Of M.P. on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173051601/
1 to the police; the prosecutrix did not speak a word about commission of rape to the Mandideep police while they stayed with it from 7.1.1997 un til 11.1.1997; there was no independent corroboration from any prosecution witness; even the landlord of the rented room failed to give support to the prosecution case.

sentences.text: On the basis of these grounds, it was requested that the appeal should be allowed and the accused persons should be acquitted.
4. State has opposed this criminal appeal claiming that the impugned judgment warrants no interference.
5. The counsel for both the parties have been heard and record of the trial court has been perused.
6. In this case, it is claimed that two minor girls left their Sanstha on their own initiative; left Jabalpur for Mandideep;
the two accused persons met and stalked them in Mandideep and later offered to show them a rented house as both the girls were looking for it for their stay in Mandideep.

It is further claimed that both the accused persons committed rape with these girls on the same night and insisted that one of the girls should marry a third person, this third person gave 3 CRA-1339-1998 information to the police upon which police came into action and took both the prosecutrix into its protection.

These facts disclose that the girls left their Sanstha on 4.1.1997 and they were taken into its protection by Mandideep police on 7.1.1997.
7.
The facts discussed above reveal that both the prosecutrix had arrived Mandideep on 5.1.1997 and they were allegedly in the company of accused persons from 5.1.1997 till 7.1.1997.
These prosecutrices were examined in the case as P.W.4 and P.W.5.

Their claim was that they were raped by accused persons on the night of 5.1.1997 and in the next morning they were taken by accused persons to Bhopal where they watched the movie and later came back to their rented house in Mandideep.
Both these girls never complained to anyone about the crime which was being committed with them.
They were not so naive that they couldn't assess their conditions.

They had left their Sanstha of Jabalpur and had travelled to Mandideep with an object to be independent and self-reliant, therefore it cannot be claimed that they could not assess that they were being sexually abused.
Still, they did not complain to anyone either during their stay in Mandideep or during their visit to Bhopal.
8. Shyamlal (P.W.6) is the landlord whose room was rented for these two girls.

His testimony reveals that no complaint was made by both these girls either to this witness or to his wife nor they heard any screams of the prosecutrices when they were being allegedly raped in his rented room.
He also admitted that there were three adjoining rooms to the one that was given on rent to the girls.
9. The prosecution case fails to inspire confidence not only on the basis of foregoing discussion but also for the reason that there was exceptional delay in reporting the matter to the police.

Admittedly,
the prosecutrices were under the 4 CRA-1339-1998 protection of police ever since 7.1.1997 but the report in the matter was made to the police on 17.1.1997.
This delay makes the matter more unreliable and creates the impression that prosecutrices were purposely hiding truth from the officials of their Sanstha and also from the police.

sentences.text: Now, let us examine whether the prosecution has been able to prove that both the prosecutrices were minor at the time of commission of alleged crime.
There is no school record or birth certificate produced in the case to prove the date of birth of prosecutrices.

According to Mohini Dubey (P.W.1),
who was Superintendent of the concerned Sanstha where the prosecutrices were housed, both these girls had arrived in that Sanstha just two years prior to the incident. She has admitted in her cross-examination that the ages of inmates are recorded in the Sanstha on the basis of information given by the person or the police who brings the minors to the Sanstha.
These statements reflect that the concerned Sanstha or its office bearers had no definite knowledge about the age or dates of birth of the prosecutrices.

In these circumstances, the ossification test report would have been the most reliable document to establish the age of prosecutrices at the time of incident but no such evidence was produced by prosecution as is evident from the record.
Dr. (Smt.) S. Chakraverty had medically examined both the prosecutrices and had referred them to the Radiologist for their age determination but there is no report of Radiologist on that point.
11. The facts discussed above reveal that the prosecution took no measures to establish that the age of prosecutrices were below 16 years at the time of commission of this crime in the year 1997.
In that period, the age of consent was 16 years.

Thus, a sexual intercourse with a girl of less than 16 years even with her consent was a crime but establishing physical relationship with a girl of 16 years or more with her consent did not fall into the category of crime.
Here, the age of 5 CRA-1339-1998 both the prosecutrices have not proved to be below 16.
Further, their conduct has already been discussed revealing that they did not make any complaint despite having several opportunities to raise alarm against their sexual harassment.

Their silence testifies to their consent and a consenting sexual act with a girl of 16 years or more could not have been categorised as a crime in the given period of time.
12.
Consequently, this appeal is allowed and the accused persons are acquitted of the charge of Section 376(1) IPC.
13. The accused persons are on bail.
Their bail-bonds stand discharged.
14. A copy of this judgment along with its record be send to the trial court for information and necessary compliance.
